<section class="site-hero">
  <div class="hub-kicker">Architecture 2.0 Evaluation Portal</div>
  <h1>AI-Native Design Benchmarks</h1>
  <p class="subtitle">Standard evaluation targets for AI-native chip and systems design loops</p>
</section>

<p class="site-lede">
In Architecture 2.0, the object of study is the <strong>AI-native design system</strong>—the configured ensemble of learned models, conventional simulators, verification checks, and tool feedback loops. Unlike classical architecture suites that benchmark conventional silicon chips, these benchmarks evaluate the AI design loop itself: specification-to-RTL generators, closed-loop debuggers, learned EDA surrogates, and autonomous design space exploration.
</p>

<div class="registry-legend" aria-label="Portal governance">
  <strong>Architecture 2.0 evaluation standards (<a href="/book/contents/chapters/10-evaluation/10-evaluation.html#sec-evaluation-objects">Chapter 10</a>)</strong>
  <span><b>Evaluation objects:</b> every card separates claims about the <i>candidate design</i>, a <i>learned component</i>, the <i>configured system</i>, or the <i>complete workflow</i>.</span>
  <span><b>Matched comparators:</b> automated workflows must report matching non-learned baselines at equal compute budgets (<i>C</i><sub>workflow</sub> = &lang;<i>C</i><sub>compute</sub>, <i>C</i><sub>license</sub>, <i>C</i><sub>human</sub>&rang;).</span>
  <span><b>Contamination &amp; health:</b> raw pass rates require contamination screening (CDD) and testbench stimulus sensitivity checks.</span>
</div>
